cards.back: m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) — rise over run, keep both differences in the same order.
y = mx + c: m gradient, c the y-intercept.
Parallel: equal gradients. Perpendicular: m₁ × m₂ = −1 — negative reciprocals.
y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) — use when a point and the gradient are known.

cards.front: Axis of symmetry of a parabola
cards.back: x = −b/2a — also the x-coordinate of the vertex; substitute back for y.
Δ > 0 two distinct real roots · Δ = 0 one repeated root · Δ < 0 no real roots.

cards.front: Vertex form y = a(x − h)² + k — what it tells you
cards.back: Vertex (h, k) — note the sign flip of h. a > 0 → minimum, a < 0 → maximum.
OUTSIDE changes y (as written): f(x)+a up, a·f(x) vertical stretch. INSIDE changes x (opposite): f(x−a) right, f(ax) horizontal compression ½.
One output per input — fails the vertical line test otherwise. ±√x is NOT a function.
Domain = allowed inputs (denominator ≠ 0, square root ≥ 0). Range = possible outputs.
f(g(x)): work inside-out. f(g(2)) means g first, then f.
Swap x and y, solve for y. Graph mirrors in y = x. (f ∘ f⁻¹)(x) = x.
The function must pass the horizontal line test — restrict the domain if it doesn't (e.g. x² on x ≥ 0).
y = f′(a)(x − a) + f(a) — gradient f′(a), through the point (a, f(a)).
Paper 1: exact algebra — no GDC. Paper 2: GDC allowed, use the graphing calculator to verify roots and intercepts.
Shape (a sign), y-intercept, axis of symmetry, vertex with coordinates, roots. Label everything — sketch marks are for labels.
The x-coordinates of the intersection points — GDC: use intersect, report ALL solutions.
State = read off, no working. Find = show method or GDC steps. The verb decides how much working earns marks.
Zoom windows can hide intersection points — set the window first or use the solver with sensible bounds; always report ALL solutions.
